sections.h2: Who bills and collects property tax in Henderson County, KY?
sections.html:
The Henderson County Sheriff's Office mails and collects the bill, the Property Valuation Administrator (PVA) sets the value it is based on, and the County Clerk's Office takes over bills that go unpaid. Each step has its own counter in the Henderson area, so a seller needs to know which one holds the file.

The county's tax collection FAQ says real estate notices go out in late October or early November and can be paid to the sheriff beginning November 1. A bill becomes delinquent on January 1 following its due date. The sheriff keeps collecting until the uncollected bills are turned over to the county clerk, who holds them from then on.

The PVA decides what your parcel is worth. A dispute over value goes through the appeal steps described below, and a bill that has not arrived is a question for the sheriff's office.

sections.h2: What should a seller know about Henderson County itself?
sections.html:
Henderson County is a western Kentucky county on the Ohio River, directly across from Evansville, Indiana, and it belongs to the Evansville, IN-KY metropolitan area. It was created from Christian County in December 1798 and took its name from Richard Henderson of the Transylvania Company. The county seat and largest city is Henderson, which began as a settlement called Red Banks.

The county measures 466 square miles, about 30 of them water, and the Wikipedia profile places it in the West Kentucky Coal Field. Other incorporated places are Corydon and Robards, and Anthoston, Poole and Spottsville are census-designated places. A stretch of roughly 45 square miles known as Green River Island lies on the Indiana side of the river but is part of Henderson County, where Ellis Park Race Course sits.

Henderson was once the largest dark tobacco market in the world, with 17 stemmeries in the city around 1880. Tobacco production fell through the twentieth century. Census figures for 2022 show about $763 million in retail sales and about $312 million in health care and social assistance receipts. The county's 2020 census count of 44,793 was down 3.2 percent from 2010, so listings face a market that is steady and not fast-growing.

sections.h2: How do Henderson County housing numbers compare?
sections.html:
The typical Henderson County home is valued above Hart County's $146,000 and below Henry County's $197,900, and 37 percent of occupied homes were rented at the 2020 census.

sections.h2: What happens if a Henderson County tax bill goes delinquent?
sections.html:
Interest and penalties start running, a lien attaches, and someone else can buy the debt. The Henderson County Attorney's tax collection FAQ walks through the sequence.

  • Delinquent bills move to the County Clerk's Office, 20 N Main Street, 2nd Floor, Henderson, and accrue interest of 1 percent per month plus penalties until paid.
  • A lien stays on the property until the bill is paid in full.
  • Any individual or company qualified under KRS Chapter 134 can buy the bill at the clerk's tax sale. The clerk can neither predict nor block that purchase.
  • The buyer has 50 days to notify you. After that you pay the buyer, who sends a release to the clerk for recording.
  • The buyer may file a foreclosure action one year after the certificate of delinquency was created.

The clerk's office takes full payment by mail in the form of a personal check, cashier's check, money order or certified check. It accepts American Express, Discover and MasterCard, plus Visa as a debit, with a small added fee; the number to call is 270-827-5753.

sections.h2: How do I contest a Henderson County assessment?
sections.html:
Request a conference with the PVA or a deputy first, because the law makes that step a precondition to any appeal. Under KRS 133.120 the conference must take place before or during the tax roll inspection period, unless the Department of Revenue approves an extension of up to 25 days.

A paid representative at the conference or the hearing must fall in one of the statutory categories, including an attorney, a certified public accountant, a tax consultant, an employee of the owner, a Kentucky real estate broker or sales associate, or a certified Kentucky real property appraiser. The representative has to present written authorization and disclose any contingency fee, though attorneys need not state the terms.

If the conference does not settle it, file a written petition with the county clerk by one workday after inspection ends. The board then holds a public hearing for each appeal and fixes the value at fair cash value. The county attorney appears for the state and county, and the Department of Revenue may attend. A person who loses before the board may take the case to the Board of Tax Appeals, but only if they appeared before the county board first.

The board can also raise a value. If it considers an increase, it must send notice with a hearing date so the owner can protest.

sections.h2: Is the homestead exemption available in Henderson County?
sections.html:
Yes, for owners who are 65 or older or totally disabled and who live in the house. The Department of Revenue's figure for the 2025 and 2026 assessment years is $49,100, applied to the assessed value of the home.

Applied to the $171,900 Census median for Henderson County, the exemption leaves $122,800 as the taxable base. Submit the application to the Henderson County PVA with proof of age, such as a birth certificate, driver's license or passport. Owners claiming through disability must show total disability under a federal program or a retirement system, and must reapply every year unless they are service-connected veterans or hold a permanent disability ruling from Social Security or Kentucky Retirement Systems.

sections.h2: How are taxes handled when a Henderson County house closes?
sections.html:
The tax bill for a year belongs to the person who owned the property on January 1, and the debt follows the land if it is not paid. KRS 134.015(4) and (5) make the tax a personal debt of that owner and keep a delinquency lien alive under KRS 134.420 for eleven years regardless of ownership changes.

At closing, the title agent usually checks the sheriff's file, and any open balance with the clerk, then pays it from your proceeds. If the previous year's bill is unpaid and sitting at the clerk's office, expect the 1 percent monthly interest to be part of the payoff figure.

The grantor also pays Kentucky's transfer tax of $0.50 per $500 of value under KRS 142.050. The Henderson County Clerk collects it when the deed is presented, and on a $171,900 sale it comes to $172.

faqs.q: When can I start paying my Henderson County property tax?
faqs.a: November 1. The sheriff's office mails notices in late October or early November, and payment to the sheriff opens on November 1. The bill turns delinquent on January 1.

faqs.q: Where do I pay a delinquent Henderson County tax bill?
faqs.a: At the County Clerk's Office, 20 N Main Street, 2nd Floor Offices, Henderson, KY 42420, or by mailing a check, money order or other certified funds to that address.

faqs.q: How much interest accrues on a delinquent Henderson County bill?
faqs.a: One percent per month, plus penalties, once the bill sits in the clerk's office. A buyer of the bill at the tax sale can add the charges Kentucky law allows.

faqs.q: Does the Henderson County homestead exemption need to be renewed?
faqs.a: An age-based exemption carries forward. A disability-based one must be renewed yearly unless the owner is a service-connected veteran or has a permanent disability ruling.

faqs.q: What transfer tax applies to a Henderson County deed?
faqs.a: Fifty cents for each $500 of value or fraction of it, paid by the grantor and collected by the clerk before the deed is recorded.
